title: A Spire for the Ember Anew
premise: Rosalind Quintana keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Meridian, a guild that trades in impossible things, while hiding her gift for speaking with beasts—a crime punishable by burning. When she discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies, she and the guild are dragged into a dying covenant between the human city of Vantrell and the beast-realm of Ashfall, one that a long winter is already devouring. To survive, Rosalind must reforge the covenant by confessing her forbidden gift before the assembled guilds, choosing truth over the loyalty that has kept her alive. The covenant is renewed at terrible cost—her mentor's life, her place in the guild—but winter breaks, and Rosalind leaves to become the first sworn envoy between realms.
about_author: Felix Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing trade ledgers from defunct merchant guilds, an obsession that bleeds into every page of his fiction. He writes fantasy about people caught between institutions and their consciences, and lives quietly where the winters are long enough to be characters.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She audits the Gilded Meridian's strangest entries—a caged storm, a vial of borrowed luck—while secretly soothing the guild's beasts in the cellar, her gift a hanging offense. Her mentor Corvane warns her that the Prophecy Ledger, untouched for a century, has begun writing again. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; the sense that safety is a debt coming due.

chapters.title: Tonight's Date
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She finds today's date inked in the Prophecy Ledger beside a line about 'the ember anew,' and before she can hide it, the guild's enforcers arrive with a captured creature from Ashfall that speaks her name. Corvane buys her silence; the creature, a fox-thing called Sennet, begs her to listen. Emotional beat: vertigo—the future reaching backward to claim her.

chapters.title: What the Fox Owes
chapters.summary: Sennet's POV. He explains the covenant: a hundred years ago, Vantrell and Ashfall bound themselves so each realm could survive the other's excesses, and the bond is failing as the long winter falls. He was sent to find 'the speaker' named in the prophecy—and Rosalind is the only beast-speaker alive. Emotional beat: reluctant kinship; two fugitives recognizing each other's chains.

chapters.title: The Guild's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Meridian's masters learn what she is and, rather than burn her, decide to sell her—to the rival Cinder Compact, who want the covenant dead so they can strip Ashfall bare. Corvane votes with them. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into clarity; loyalty revealed as a ledger with her name on the debit side.

chapters.title: Out the Coal Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Sennet flee through the guild's smuggling tunnels with enforcers behind them, guided by rats whose chatter Rosalind alone can parse. They surface in the frozen sprawl outside Vantrell's walls, where the winter is visibly wrong—snow falling upward at the boundary of Ashfall. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into resolve on open ground.

chapters.title: The Border That Breathes
chapters.summary: Sennet's POV. Crossing into Ashfall, they find the realm starving and half-mad with cold, its great beasts turning on smaller ones as the covenant's protections fail. Sennet must choose between delivering Rosalind to the Ember Court as the prophecy demands or shielding her from a court that may see her as an omen to kill. Emotional beat: love tested against duty for the first time.

chapters.title: Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Before the Ember Court, she learns the covenant's original terms: it was sealed with a beast-speaker's willing voice, and only such a voice can renew it. The Court offers her sanctuary if she stays forever as their living seal—an elegant cage. Emotional beat: temptation; survival offered at the price of becoming a thing kept.

chapters.title: The Compact Marches
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The Cinder Compact breaches the border with fire-oil and hired blades, intending to kill the court and let both realms freeze into exploitable ruin. Corvane arrives among them—not as captor but as penitent, carrying the stolen Prophecy Ledger and a confession he means to speak aloud. Emotional beat: collision; every debt arriving at once.

chapters.title: A Voice Given Freely
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the breaking covenant-stone, with the Compact closing in, Rosalind publicly names her gift before humans and beasts alike—the confession that once meant burning—and speaks the renewal. Corvane dies holding the Compact's captain back from her; Sennet takes wounds meant for her. The covenant catches like struck flint. Emotional beat: climax—truth costing everything and buying the dawn.

chapters.title: Ember Anew
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Winter recedes; the Compact's leaders face guild justice, and the Meridian, gutted by scandal, offers Rosalind anything to stay. Instead she accepts the first-ever post of sworn envoy between realms, with Sennet as her counterpart. Final beat: bittersweet ascent—she lost her old life to gain a truer one, and walks the thawing border unafraid.
